title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists activate rodent thyroid C-cells causing calcitonin release and C-cell proliferation
authors: Bjerre Knudsen L, Madsen LW, Andersen S, Almholt K, de Boer AS, Drucker DJ, et al.
population: Rats, mice, cynomolgus monkeys, human thyroid tissue and patients in liraglutide trials
funder: No separate funding statement was found in the archived full text; the disclosure states that all authors except D.J.D. were employees of Novo Nordisk, most of them minor shareholders, that Novo Nordisk is developing liraglutide, and that manuscript assistance from Watermeadow Medical was supported by Novo Nordisk A/S; D.J.D. received research grant support from Novo Nordisk.
authorConflicts: D.J.D. reported advisory or consulting relationships with Novo Nordisk, Eli Lilly and other manufacturers.
result: The GLP-1 receptor was localised to rodent thyroid C cells; GLP-1 receptor agonists stimulated calcitonin release, raised calcitonin gene expression and then caused C-cell hyperplasia in rats and, to a lesser extent, mice. Human and cynomolgus monkey C cells had low GLP-1 receptor expression, and agonists did not activate adenylate cyclase or release calcitonin in primates; 20 months of liraglutide at more than 60 times human exposure caused no C-cell hyperplasia in monkeys. Mean calcitonin in patients on liraglutide for 2 years stayed at the lower end of normal. The authors state that the long-term consequences of sustained GLP-1 receptor activation in the human thyroid remain unknown.
